sequencing_rationale: QA REFRAMING (stated explicitly because the intake evidence is borrowed): the intake describes this as a course for the 'indentured website developer apprentice'. It is a shared web-development course repurposed for the Quality Assurance Software Engineer pathway, so this outline teaches toward the QA catalog. The QA framing is that computational thinking is test-design thinking: partitioning an input space is the same skill as choosing equivalence classes, boundary reasoning around a binary search midpoint is the same skill as boundary-value analysis, complexity is how you predict where a performance test will hurt, and the data structures in lesson 03 are framed as the shapes a defect record or a test-data fixture is actually stored in (D3-S1-C05). Lesson 06 frames traversal as walking a DOM or dependency tree to isolate a failure (D3-S1-C02), and lesson 07 turns the whole course into deliberate test-data design ahead of a change being validated (D4-S1-C03). SEQUENCE: thinking, then structures, then search, then sort, then traversal, then complexity and test data. Structures precede algorithms because an algorithm's cost is a property of the structure it runs over; complexity comes last so it can be stated over algorithms the learner has already implemented. SCOPE ASSUMPTIONS, derived from the title, the 20 authored hours, and the surviving description fragment: the description is truncated mid-word ('binary searc'), and 'graph transversals' is read as 'graph traversals'. The fragment names data sorting, computational thinking, graph traversal, and binary search, and those four drive lessons 02 and 04 to 06; nothing was invented to complete the cut-off sentence. The intake says the course uses HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to teach these topics, so all worked examples are plain JavaScript, with the browser used only for display. Assumed in scope: decomposition and pseudocode, arrays, linked lists, maps and sets, linear and binary search, at least one quadratic and one divide-and-conquer sort, tree and graph traversal (depth-first and breadth-first), and big-O reasoning at an introductory level. Assumed out of scope and deliberately left out: heaps, tries, dynamic programming, amortized analysis, and formal proofs of correctness. HOURS: 1h overview plus six lessons of 3 to 3.5h, summing to exactly 20. LESSON KINDS: intake records no project count for this course, so lesson 07 is a taught lesson with an extended hands-on Practice rather than a graded project brief.

proposed_competencies.competency_text: The learner can reason about an algorithm's cost to predict where a change carries performance risk and target testing accordingly.
proposed_competencies.rationale: Lesson 07 uses complexity to decide what to test and with how much data. D4-S1-C04 covers planning test schedules and strategies against scope and delivery dates, but the catalog has no competency about risk-based prioritisation driven by how the code will actually behave at scale.
